name: Galu
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Only Laycock 1968 1-page wordlist per Glottolog MED; no grammar/phonology exists

new_statements.quote: In general the lower of the above vocoid phones is to be understood. Stress is marked only if it falls on other than the first syllable not containing [ə]. Stress does not appear to be a phonemic feature in any of these languages. The entire question of the phonemic interpretation of suspicious vocoid sequences is very complex and no consistency should be expected in the transcription.
new_statements.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1968. Languages of the Lumi Subdistrict (West Sepik District), New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 7(1): 36-66. doi:10.2307/3622846
new_statements.locator: Introduction, transcription conventions, immediately before 'The phonological summary is tentative in all instances given.' and the heading 'A. WAPEI-PALEI PHYLUM' (article pp. 36-66; printed page not resolved by the archive.org API, c. pp. 39-41). Galu entry = language no. 13 of the list, p. 48 (Glottolog subclassification comment 'Laycock 1968: 48'; Laycock 1973:10 'see Laycock (1968:13)').
new_statements.rule_in_words: Survey-wide convention applied to every Lumi-Subdistrict wordlist including Galu: stress is non-phonemic and by default falls on the first syllable of the word whose vowel is not schwa; only deviations from that default are marked, and none of the 38 Galu forms is marked (e.g. nəmo 'cat' would be stressed on -mo, rakita 'arm' on ra-).
new_statements.exceptions: Any word stressed elsewhere than the first non-schwa syllable would carry a stress mark; in the Galu list as re-keyed on TransNewGuinea.org no form is marked. Laycock warns that the transcription of vocoid sequences is inconsistent and that every phonological summary is tentative.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms from a single elicited test wordlist (DCL67, ~40 items) recorded at Nuku, July 1967; the statement is a transcription convention for the whole survey, not an analysis of Galu, and it is obtained only as scanned snippets of a print-disabled scan.
new_statements.identity_note: The only stress statement is a survey-wide transcription convention in Laycock 1968 that covers all ~60 Lumi-Subdistrict wordlists at once; Galu is language no. 13 of that list (entry at printed p. 48 per Glottolog's subclassification comment; Laycock 1973:10 cross-refers to 'Laycock (1968:13)'), recorded from informants Pokon and Timpien of Weiki and Einofi of Wara at Nuku, July 1967. Laycock lists Galu under the names Metru and Sinagen; Laycock 1973 treats Galu (entry 23) as distinct from Alu/Dia (entry 22, 'Alu (Dia, Metru, Sinagen)', Glottolog alud1235? -- Glottolog's Galu-Alu group galu1240 holds both). There is no Galu-specific phonological remark anywhere.
